Mr Wheelchair Fraud

By: Jacqui Jayamaha | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Wheelchair bound people depend on mobility aids such as hoists to make their lives easier however a supplier of this equipment is blatantly defrauding his clients.

Unique Selling Point:
We investigate a case of fraud against Mr Wheelchair director, Martin Visagie, who is charging outlandish amounts of money for supplying mobility aids to people with disabilities. He promises state of the art equipment but supplies second grade, used gear or worse doesn't deliver what was promised even after full payment. Quad Para Association of SA has received numerous complaints about Visagie.

Summary:
Single mother Marie Marais is quadriplegic and rising her 2 sons on her own. She paid Visagie R98 000 almost 2 years ago for a pool hoist which would allow her to get into the water with her boys. She is still waiting for the equipment. Visagie ignores her countless please to install the hoist as paid for. Jeweller Paddy Fitzpatrick is 74 years old and was a victim of polio as a baby. He paid R90 000 to Visagie for a car hoist in order for him to drive to work but what was installed was a 14 year old, hugely over priced and unsafe device.
We talk to these vulnerable people and confront the supplier Visagie once the evidence is collected

Script:


Mr. Wheel Chair (10 minutes)

V/O After a horrific car accident in 1994, Maria Marais’ injuries left her quadriplegic. She is a single mother of 2 active, young boys.

Int Maria I’m a C5, C6 quadriplegic, which basically means I’ve lost function from my chest down.

Devi, Being a mom is tough enough and you also have to deal with the fact that you’re in a wheel chair?
Int Maria There’s a lot I can’t do with the kids and I try to teach them through my experiences that you set your own limits; you are the one that decides how far you’re going to push yourself.
VO Marais needs assistance with most daily activities.

Link “Maria decided that she needed to become more independent and to do that she needed a hoist which would allow her to get in and out of bed by herself. She also wanted a pool hoist, she looked online and it seemed Mr Wheelchair in Pinetown was the man for the job.

V/O Martin Visagie is the owner of Mr. Wheelchair, a local mobility aid supplier.

Int Maria I looked on the website, he was the first one that popped up, when I realised he was in a wheelchair himself, I thought he was someone who will understand my situation.
V/O A couch and pool hoist were ordered
Devi And how much was it going to cost you?
Int Maria He gave me a quote of R98 000. He did get the money in July 2017.
V/O The pool hoist was of primary importance to her.
Int Maria My goal had been to have it here by the December holidays so I that could be in the pool with the kids.
V/O A pool lift would allow for easy transfer from the wheelchair into the water.

V/O Marias Christmas wish was not realised - the pool hoist was only installed 6 months after payment in July 2017, it didn’t work then, it’s rusting and still doesn’t work now.

Devi” Even if you wanted you couldn’t get yourself off here, because it’s stuck
Int Maria And it cannot lift to move over so its stuck there you can’t go anywhere with it.

Int Maria Ah, He promising to sort things out and nothing happens.
V/O Marias showed us the latest mail to Mr. Wheelchair dated February 2019 appealing for him to come and replace her hoist as was agreed.

Link “The hardship of being mobility impaired is something that no-one can fully prepare for, especially the endless medical expenses.
V/O Another unhappy Mr. Wheelchair client is 75-year-old jeweler, Paddy Fitzpatrick.
Int Paddy “Well quite frankly I’ve given up any hope redeeming money out of Martin
Int Paddy Because I bought a new vehicle, I needed to get into my car from a wheelchair and maneuver myself into a position where I was in front of the wheel, the driver’s wheel.
V/O A car lift is intended to transfer the wheelchair-bound driver into the car and into the drivers seat.
Int Paddy Independence is the greatest thing that you can give any body, doesn’t matter if you’re old you’re disabled, independence is of absolute of vital importance
V/O Fitzpatrick ordered a new lift for R120 000, as reflected on his letter, instead he got a demo model that was an old design, it didn’t get him behind the wheel.

Int Victor Whoever was selling that I don’t know what they were thinking, that’s ludicrous, even the imported lifts aren’t that price.
V/O In the local mobility aid industry for 22 years, Victor Panaino, Director of Skyjacks, recently saw Paddy’s vehicle and identified the car hoist as one of his much older designs.
Int Victor When I first saw the lift I knew it was an older model and then I saw the new type of flap that we do now put onto the lift and as I looked at it realised this thing was bastardised, if I can use that word.
V/O Paddy had a bad fall off the lift.
Int Paddy So I got to the edge and I touched the pushed the toggle here which pushed it forward and I shot over the edge and I say I bliksemed over the ramp.
Int Victor So I’m concerned the guys can sell it in the market like that and not care about people’s safety it’s a little bit scary, I realised there’s nothing we can do, we can’t even fix it we have to replace the lift there’s no way we can fix it”.
V/O ”Panaino had designed the model used by Visagie in Paddy’s car in 2004, making it over 15 years old. Back then it retailed at around R30 000
Int Victor Brand new out of the box lift, with a guarantee is R61 000 now.

V/O Afflicted by polio as a baby, Fitzpatrick has spent his life in a wheelchair. His wife Sabrina says her frustration and anger towards Visagie has reached boiling point.
Sabrina It was absolute lies from the beginning to the end, and that’s why I’m so glad you’re here today because I think people out there need to know that, he doesn’t care, he actually doesn’t care for the situations that we find ourselves in.

V/O Ari Seirlis, CEO of QuadPara Association of South Africa, is aware of the serious problems many mobility challenged people are having with Visagie.

Int Ari We do get a tremendous amount of complaints about Mr. Wheelchair, and it concerns us, and it concerns me. In my opinion certainly he’s not getting his business from being known as a fair trader or good service.
This story worries me terribly …and if I was that client or consumer, I’d be absolutely furious knowing the facts that I know.

V/O We sent in our undercover operatives posing as potential clients to meet Visagie and find out about the promises he makes.

Ryan How long does it take after we order the stuff?
Visagie Ok this will take about 4 weeks, 6 weeks, within that time ya.
Jack “So its quite quick
Jack Car lift, pool lift, bath lift.
Ryan And deposit wise
Visagie On these ones because it’s imported so we’re going to need 75%
Jack “We’re looking around R220 R250
Visagie “Correct…It’s international standard; it’s a high standard.
Jack - And these things are all new, brand new?
Visagie “Brand new”.
Visagie “For us once its done and its finished you know that special smile, you that it makes my life better…that’s the payment, you know that’s the real payment”.

V/O We didn’t see any special smiles from Marias and the Fitzpatricks, so we returned to the workshop to confront Visagie.

Devi Hi Martin, Devi Carte Blanche, how are you?
Int Martin No fine and you?
Devi I’m good, I’m good. So we’ve heard a couple of complaints, I want to hear your side of the story.
Int Martin Of course ya.
Devi Ok Martin, let’s quickly start, first of all with Maria Marais,
Int Martin Ya
Devi She wanted, if you could remember?
Int Martin A pool hoist
Devi It was full payment R98 000?
Devi The money was paid in full around July 2017.
Int Martin Yes
Devi That’s 2 years ago.
Int Martin Ya
Devi Why has it taken so long for the complaints to be resolved?
Int Martin Because we’ve continually adjusted it.
Devi I went to her house yesterday
Int Martin Ya
Devi The pool hoist doesn’t work.

Int Martin It works 100%, there’s no problem with it.
Devi If it worked she would be in the pool.
Int Martin My mechanic fitted the seals and the seals was wrongly fitted, I’ve sent it to an engineering company they fitted new seals we went back to her, we’ve installed it and it works 100%.
Int Martin She might not know how it works, however
Devi No, no I think she would know how it works
Int Martin Ok
Devi She’s a smart lady.
Int Martin Ya, ok
Devi It’s rusting
Int Martin It’s not rusting
Devi I saw it, I know what’s rust, I come from KZN!
Int Martin The grinder had some er, mild steel on it, on the blade itself and some of that fine filings stayed behind on the actual pole, it’s 316 it can’t rust.
Devi So is t rust, or is it not rust?
Int Martin It’s not rust!
Devi Are you not concerned that I’m telling you that the pool hoist doesn’t work?
Int Martin I am concerned about that.
Devi Paddy Fitzpatrick, what went wrong?
Int Martin I’m not sure I don’t have the documents with me.
Devi I’ve got it, here’s the invoice.
V/O To jog his memory we handed him his invoice for Fitzpatricks car hoist.
Devi The supply and fitment of single arm hydraulic lift.
Int Martin That was in the shop as a demonstration model, and he knew that
Devi So was he going to get a brand new one?
Int Martin No we were going to use that one, which we did.
V/O We let Visagie know that the designer of the car lift confirmed it was 15 years old.
Devi The latest car hoist you can buy for R60 000, are you aware of that?
Martin Int A little bit more than that! But yes.
Devi A little bit more is what? R70 000?
Int Martin Ya call it R70 000
Devi Why you charge these people R120 000 for a 15-year-old model?
Int Martin Paddy looked at it Paddy was quite happy with it, and that was the only hoist that at that particular time that would fit that door.
Devi Remember this is going on TV, other people are going to look at these numbers, and what do you think they are gong to say Martin? Would they say that this is fair?
Int Martin Well this sounds, these sounds now, like not fair,
Devi So why did you do this to these people?
Int Martin To my satisfaction I think that we’ve done it the right way, I do believe we’ve done it the right way.
V/O But Mr. Wheelchair’s clients still want their money’s worth.
Int Paddy He’s in a wheelchair and you’d think there would be empathy towards people who are in the same predicament as what he is in.
Int Maria I’m not a fighter but what Martin has done is wrong, and I feel that when a person does an injustice to somebody there’s got to come a time where they’ve got to answer to that”

V/O in a subsequent telephone conversation, Visagie said he would return all the money to Marais and Fitzpatrick within a week and apologised.

Recorded Phone call “
Martin What I’ve decided is this, I’m going to give both the customers their money back.
Jack Fantastic when would we expect you to do that?
Martin Within one week, I’m very sorry about this whole thing.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


11 sec teasers x 3

• A rusting pool hoist and ineffective car lift that cost a fortune… how did one supplier of mobility aids in Durban let his wheelchair-bound customers down?

• The price-tag was a staggering R120,000 for a car hoist that doesn’t do what it was supposed to – how has one wheelchair-bound client been let down by a supplier of mobility aids?

• Over-priced and under-delivered – how a Durban mobility aid supplier has exploited his wheelchair-bound clients. (Sound up Maria) “Ah he keeps promising to sort things out and nothing happens”
